question.text: Mr. Vivek Kaushik, the Compliance Officer at 'Narmada Capital AIF', is considering the legal risk in side letter enforceability. What does the chapter state about side letter enforceability in India?

answer.text: Side letters are directly enforceable under the SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012
Side letters are treated as secondary contracts under the Indian Contract Act, 1872 with full enforceability
Only those side letters registered with SEBI are enforceable
Side letter enforceability has not been tested adequately in Indian courts and they do carry a certain amount of legal risk

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 13.4.1, side letter enforceability has not been tested adequately in Indian courts and they do have a certain amount of legal risk for such investors. This is material when negotiating with foreign investors used to common-law jurisdictions where side letter enforceability is well-settled. The Trap: SEBI (AIF) Regulations don't specifically enforce side letters — they are bilateral contracts. SEBI registration of side letters is not a feature of the regulations. Cross-Exam Context: IA Level 2 (X-B) and PMS (XXI-B) don't deal with side letters. XIX-C is the only exam that drills into this private-fund-specific legal risk. Manager's Pro-Tip: For foreign LPs, consider an arbitration clause with seat in Singapore/London and governing law of a common-law jurisdiction — mitigates the Indian enforceability risk materially.
